answer: A farm scripting its whole army of identities fires them together, thus the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 58 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. The sparrow detector writes to umber, and gale shows every merge. Submissions that land within 155 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. That is 10 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
